question: In adults with a synthetic chronic condition, does Treatment A reduce the fictional biomarker compared with usual care?

provenance.note: All records and results are fictional, authored for software testing.

studies.title: Synthetic randomized trial of Treatment A
studies.abstract: In this fictional randomized study of 240 adults, Treatment A reduced the fictional biomarker by 8 units versus 3 units with usual care at 12 weeks. Attrition was 18%, and the study was not powered for clinical outcomes.

studies.title: Synthetic observational study of Treatment A
studies.abstract: In this fictional cohort of 1,100 adults, Treatment A was associated with a 4-unit larger biomarker reduction after adjustment. Residual confounding and incomplete outcome capture were possible.

studies.title: Synthetic null trial of Treatment A on the biomarker
studies.abstract: In this fictional randomized trial of 90 adults, Treatment A showed no biomarker difference versus usual care at 6 weeks. The confidence interval was wide and the follow-up shorter than in the other trial.

studies.title: Synthetic inhaler trial for asthma symptoms
studies.abstract: In a fictional asthma trial, inhaler B improved symptom scores over 8 weeks. Hospital admissions were not measured.

studies.title: Synthetic blood pressure study of exercise
studies.abstract: In a fictional exercise cohort, weekly walking was associated with lower blood pressure. Participants selected their own exercise, and confounding by baseline fitness was possible.

studies.title: Synthetic diabetes screening evaluation
studies.abstract: In this fictional diabetes screening evaluation, test C had sensitivity of 80% and specificity of 70%. The sample was selected from one clinic and external validation was unavailable.

studies.title: Synthetic renal function monitoring
studies.abstract: In this fictional renal monitoring study, creatinine measurements varied across laboratories. No intervention or patient survival endpoint was studied.

studies.title: Synthetic sleep intervention pilot
studies.abstract: In this fictional sleep pilot, participants reported longer sleep after relaxation training. The study lacked a control group and used self-reported duration.
